items.title: Longitudinal pressure wave
items.text: A wave moving along a tube. Follow one particle: it only moves back and forth, while the compression travels on. (C.2.1, C.2.3)

items.title: Particle motion against propagation
items.text: The same longitudinal wave with compressions and rarefactions marked, separating what each particle does from what the wave does. (C.2.1)

items.title: Transverse wave
items.text: The particles move up and down while the wave travels left to right. (C.2.1)

items.title: Water surface wave (extra)
items.text: Particles in deep water trace circles, so a water wave is neither purely transverse nor longitudinal.

items.title: PhET: Wave on a String
items.text: Oscillate and Pulse modes, with rulers and a stopwatch to measure wavelength, amplitude and period, and sliders for amplitude, frequency, damping and tension.

items.title: An electromagnetic wave in 3D
items.alt: Animation of an electromagnetic wave in three dimensions: two sets of field vectors in perpendicular planes, both perpendicular to the direction of travel.

items.alt: Animation of an electromagnetic wave seen from the side: the electric and magnetic fields oscillating as the wave travels from left to right.

demos.title: Long slinky
demos.text: A slinky 1 m long that stretches to about 6 m. Flick one end sideways to send a transverse pulse, then push and pull the end along its length to send a longitudinal one. In each case compare which way the coils move with which way the pulse travels. (C.2.1)
